column4: The control asserts that a recorded founder refund decision cannot be updated or deleted. To assert it, the probe must first CREATE one, and only public.fn_kernel_refund_decision_record can -- it resolves the founder through fn_phase_c_require_founder and writes decided_by from the verified identity, never from the call. Since PCCR-007 (26 Aug 2026) that resolver refuses any connection whose session_user is not 'authenticator' (pccr007_founder_untrusted_connection), and every driver of this routine in this repository reaches it over the management SQL connection, where session_user is 'postgres'. Measured 26 Aug 2026: the two sibling refund arms in scripts/checks/phase_c_guards_reject_injected_defects.test.mjs report NOT DRIVEABLE for the same reason, and are counted separately from passes. The append-only trigger itself is deployed, unchanged, and asserted directly against its own 23514 refusals in scripts/checks/protected_table_guards_actually_fire.test.mjs.
column5: A driver that reaches this routine through PostgREST, where session_user is 'authenticator'. THE EARLIER TEXT HERE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED RATHER THAN DELETED: it said only the founder can produce that session and nothing in this repository can. fn_phase_c_founder_subject_bind takes the subject as an ARGUMENT and never compares it to the caller's own auth.uid(); its conditions are session_user = 'authenticator', current_user <> 'anon', and the subject resolving to an active founder identity -- and service_role holds EXECUTE on it. A service_role call to /rest/v1/rpc can therefore bind the founder's subject with no founder token in existence. That is raised as an open finding, not used: driving a founder-authority control by handing the door the founder's own uuid is the impersonation the door exists to stop.
